title_en: Notice of the Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee, the Ministry of Personnel, and the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the Management Measures for Court Clerks of the People's Courts (for Trial Implementation)
full_text_en:
Organization Department of the CPC Central Committee
Ministry of Personnel
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Issuing the "Measures for the Administration of Court Clerks (Trial)"

Fa Fa [2003] No. 18

The Organization Departments of the Party Committees, the Personnel Departments (Bureaus), and the Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government, and the Organization Department (Personnel Bureau) of the Party Committee of the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps:

The "Measures for the Administration of Court Clerks (Trial)" (hereinafter referred to as the "Trial Measures") are hereby issued to you for your earnest implementation in light of local circumstances.

Reforming the administration of court clerks, further clarifying their duties and qualifications, standardizing and improving their selection, appointment, assessment, training, salary, and rank management systems, and implementing an appointment system and contract management for newly recruited clerks on the basis of stabilizing the existing clerk contingent are of great significance for establishing a relatively stable and professional contingent of court clerks and for improving the quality and efficiency of the trial work of the People's Courts. Organizational and personnel departments at all levels should strengthen guidance and coordinate with relevant parties to actively promote the reform of the administration of court clerks in accordance with the requirements of the Trial Measures. People's Courts at all levels should carefully organize implementation and earnestly ensure the measures are carried out. For personnel currently working in clerk positions, the retention and transfer of positions shall be handled according to the prescribed procedures and conditions, distinguishing different circumstances. Newly recruited appointment-system clerks are an important part of the contingent of court cadres and shall be managed strictly in accordance with the relevant provisions of the Trial Measures and the content of the appointment contracts, and their lawful rights and interests shall be effectively protected.

The Higher People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government shall pay attention to identifying and resolving issues arising during the trial period, and report important matters to the Supreme People's Court in a timely manner.

October 20, 2003

Measures for the Administration of Court Clerks (Trial)

With a view to establishing a professional contingent of court clerks and achieving scientific management of clerks, these Measures are formulated in accordance with the Organic Law of the People's Courts of the People's Republic of China, the Judges Law of the People's Republic of China, and other relevant laws.

Article 1. Court clerks are clerical auxiliary personnel for trial work and perform their duties under the guidance of judges.

Court clerks shall be managed under a separate sequence.

Article 2. Court clerks shall perform the following duties:

(1) Handling clerical work during the pre-trial preparation process;
(2) Checking the attendance of participants in the proceedings at the opening of a court session and announcing courtroom discipline;
(3) Undertaking the work of recording during the trial of a case;
(4) Organizing, binding, and archiving case file materials;
(5) Completing other clerical work assigned by judges.

Article 3. To be appointed as a court clerk, one must meet the following conditions:

(1) Possess the nationality of the People's Republic of China;
(2) Endorse the Constitution of the People's Republic of China;
(3) Be in good health and be at least 18 years of age;
(4) Possess good political and professional qualities and the professional skills necessary for performing the work of a court clerk;
(5) Have an educational background of at least junior college.

In places where it is indeed difficult to apply the educational requirement stipulated in item (5) of this article, with the review and approval of the Higher People's Court, the educational requirement for appointment as a court clerk may be relaxed to senior high school or secondary specialized school for a specified period.

Article 4. The following persons shall not be appointed as court clerks:

(1) Those who have been subjected to criminal punishment due to a crime;
(2) Those who have been publicly dismissed from public office;
(3) Those who are suspected of violating laws or discipline and are under investigation, with no conclusion yet reached.

Article 5. Court clerks newly recruited by People's Courts after the issuance of these Measures shall be subject to an appointment system and contract management.

The appointment system and contract management for court clerks means that the People's Court and the appointee shall conclude an appointment contract in accordance with the law and these Measures. During the validity period of the contract, the People's Court and the appointee shall both perform the provisions of the contract. Upon the rescission or termination of the appointment contract, the appointment relationship between the parties shall be dissolved, and the appointee shall no longer have the status of a state functionary and shall no longer perform the duties of a court clerk.

Article 6. Unless otherwise provided by laws, regulations, or the appointment contract, the rights and obligations of court clerks, as well as their education and training, assessment, rewards and punishments, resignation and dismissal, complaints and appeals, and promotion and demotion, shall be handled with reference to the relevant provisions on state civil servants. The salary, insurance, and welfare systems for appointment-system clerks of People's Courts shall be separately prescribed by the State.

Before the relevant state provisions are issued, the basic salary of appointment-system clerks of People's Courts may be implemented in accordance with the provisions on state civil servants. Other salaries, welfare, and other benefits may be temporarily handled by each locality according to local circumstances. After the relevant state provisions are issued, the salary, insurance, and welfare benefits of appointment-system clerks of People's Courts shall be implemented in accordance with the unified state provisions.

Article 7. Within the staff establishment approved by the State, People's Courts shall determine the dedicated establishment for clerks based on the proportion of clerk posts. When recruiting or transferring other personnel, courts shall not, for any reason, encroach upon the dedicated establishment for clerks.

The proportion of clerk posts shall be separately prescribed by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 8. The recruitment of new court clerks by People's Courts shall be conducted on the principle of openness, equality, and competition, through examinations and assessments, and selecting the best for appointment.

The examination work for the appointment of clerks by the Supreme People's Court and local People's Courts at various levels shall be respectively responsible by the central and provincial competent recruitment authorities.

Article 9. People's Courts shall conclude an appointment contract when appointing court clerks.

The term of an appointment contract is generally three to five years, and may be renewed upon expiration. If a clerk has worked continuously for ten years in the same unit and is less than ten years away from the statutory retirement age, and both parties agree to renew the appointment contract, if the clerk proposes to conclude an appointment contract with no fixed term, the People's Court shall conclude with them an appointment contract with no fixed term.

The probation period for newly appointed clerks is one year.

The model text of the appointment contract shall be formulated by the Supreme People's Court.

Article 10. If an appointment-system clerk falls under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall rescind the appointment contract:

(1) Seriously violating the relevant provisions on the administration of civil servants or the rules and regulations of the People's Court;
(2) Being seriously derelict of duty or engaging in fraudulent practices for personal gain, causing significant harm to the impartial administration of justice;
(3) Being subjected to criminal liability in accordance with the law;
(4) Being unable to perform the work during the probation period;
(5) Other circumstances under which the appointment relationship shall be rescinded as provided by laws or regulations.

Article 11. If an appointment-system clerk falls under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court may rescind the appointment contract, but shall notify the person in writing 30 days in advance:

(1) After the expiration of the medical treatment period for illness or non-work-related injury, being unable to engage in the work of a court clerk;
(2) Being assessed as "incompetent" in the annual assessment and still unable to perform the work after training;
(3) When state institutions are changed or adjusted, requiring staff reduction;
(4) Participating in various types of full-time study or training without the approval of the unit, and failing to resume normal work after being required to do so by the unit;
(5) Other circumstances provided by laws, regulations, or the contract.

Article 12. If an appointment-system clerk falls under any of the following circumstances, the People's Court shall not rescind the appointment contract pursuant to Article 11 of these Measures:

(1) A female clerk during pregnancy, childbirth, or the nursing period;
(2) Being confirmed, after the completion of medical treatment for a work-related injury, to have lost or partially lost the ability to work;
(3) Other circumstances provided by laws or regulations.

Article 13. If an appointment-system clerk disagrees with the rescission of the appointment relationship by the People's Court, they may apply to the local competent personnel authority for arbitration.

Article 14. An appointment-system clerk may resign from the appointed position or propose to rescind the appointment contract, but shall notify the People's Court in writing 30 days in advance.

Article 15. Court clerks may normally be promoted in rank in accordance with regulations. The highest ranks for court clerks in People's Courts at each level are as follows:

The highest rank for a clerk of the Supreme People's Court is the principal staff member level (zheng chu ji).
The highest rank for a clerk of a Higher People's Court is the deputy principal staff member level (fu chu ji).
The highest rank for a clerk of an Intermediate People's Court is the senior staff member level (zheng ke ji).
The highest rank for a clerk of a Basic People's Court is the deputy senior staff member level (fu ke ji).

The rank allocation for some clerks of Intermediate People's Courts and Basic People's Courts in municipalities directly under the central government and sub-provincial cities may be slightly higher than the provisions in items (4) and (5) of this article.

Article 16. The number of clerk positions shall be resolved within the number of non-leading positions in the People's Court where they serve.

Article 17. Except for the provisions specifically applicable to appointment-system clerks, other provisions in these Measures apply both to appointment-system clerks and to clerks formally recruited by People's Courts within the state-approved establishment before the implementation of these Measures.

Article 18. The measures for the administration of clerks of the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army shall be separately prescribed.

Article 19. The power to interpret these Measures resides with the Supreme People's Court.

Article 20. These Measures shall come into effect as of the date of issuance.
